chapter: Kid Rena, Kelly and the old trumpeters
title: Working with Kid Rena at the Gypsy Tea Room
summary: He names early trumpeters and describes working with Kid Rena in 1932, his tone and easygoing life.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: But of course I would consider myself at that time not too much of a good judge of music or talent because I didn't know too much about it. But I could remember fellas like Buddy Petit and Sam Organ, old Sam Organ, and Chris Kelly, Kid Renee, and matter of fact I worked with Kid Renee for a while when they first opened up the New Gypsy Tea Room in 1932. Oh yeah, there on St. Philip and St. Philip.
In 1932. When they first opened up there I worked with him.

He and his brother and another fellow from the old school by the name of George Augustan. He used to play banjo at the time. As a matter of fact I think his father used to be a musician. Augustan? His father was there.
I heard that old man a lot.

Uh-huh. And out of the whole group I used to like Kid Renee very much, very much because he had very good ideas, he had a beautiful tone, and he was an inspiration to a whole lot of fellas because I remember some of the fellas used to come up there and just sit up there and watch him and listen to him and even make comments. I'd say, boy I suddenly wish I could play like that guy. But he was a happy-go-lucky fella and he didn't seem to worry about anything. He just loved to play his music and loved to have his little drink every now and then, which was more or less customary at the time. And I find that musicians in that particular area they got a lot of enjoyment out of playing and having a good time. Now whether any money was made out of the deal I don't particularly know or I don't remember. But yet still they seemed to be happy at all times. They'd never done anything but playing music. I don't think I can remember any of the fellas from the old school doing anything but playing music.
Just brought a few of them then. Yeah. Was Kid Renee your favorite trumpet would you say?
Well he was one of my favorites, yes.
